export_note: Selected fields from the completed native grade; machine-local paths are omitted. The mathematical grade is preserved.

grade.first_issue: The sufficiency proof does not justify that Mulan can force the minimum angle to become arbitrarily small regardless of which child Shan-Yu retains.
grade.summary: The characterization and necessity argument are essentially correct, and the subsequent forcing and peeling steps work once a sufficiently small angle is available. However, the proof only identifies one child with a small angle and overlooks Shan-Yu’s option to retain the other child; it also gives no finite-progress argument. This load-bearing gap is readily repairable by repeatedly bisecting an angle, since both children then contain half of it, but that argument is absent.
strengths: The safe-angle obstruction in the necessity direction correctly treats all four possible pairings.
Once an angle below \(\theta\) is secured, the supplementary-angle and peeling arguments correctly force \(\theta\).
The final set of values \(\theta=180^\circ/n\) for integers \(n\ge2\) is correct.

errors.description: The claimed ability to make the minimum angle arbitrarily small considers only the favorable child and does not establish a finite strategy against Shan-Yu’s choices.
